sections.title: Fractions, decimals & percents
facts: $p\%$ of $x$ is $\frac{p}{100} \times x$. Up $p\%$ multiplies by $1 + \frac{p}{100}$; down $p\%$ multiplies by $1 - \frac{p}{100}$.
Up $20\%$ then down $20\%$ multiplies by $1.2 \times 0.8 = 0.96$: not back to the start.
If A is $25\%$ more than B, then B is $20\%$ less than A: the difference is compared with a different number.
Repeating decimals: $0.\overline{a} = \frac{a}{9}$ and $0.\overline{ab} = \frac{ab}{99}$, so $0.\overline{36} = \frac{36}{99} = \frac{4}{11}$.
"A fraction of what is left": multiply what is left. $\frac{1}{4}$ of the remaining $\frac{2}{3}$ is $\frac{1}{6}$.

sections.title: Ratios, rates & proportions
facts: A ratio $a : b$ means $a + b$ equal parts. Find one part first: part $= \frac{\text{total}}{a + b}$.
To join $a : b$ and $b : c$, make the $b$ parts match first: $2 : 3$ and $4 : 5$ become $8 : 12 : 15$.
Rates: find the amount for ONE (one worker, one minute), then multiply up.
Units: $1$ km $= 1000$ m and $1$ hour $= 60$ minutes, so $60$ km/h is $1000$ m a minute.

sections.title: Averages
facts: Sum $=$ average $\times$ count. Turn every average into a sum.
Combine groups by their totals: $\frac{m x + k y}{m + k}$, never by averaging the averages.
Average speed $=$ total distance $\div$ total time. Same distance at speeds $u$ and $v$: $\frac{2uv}{u + v}$.
Raising the average of $n$ numbers by $d$ with one new number needs that number to be the old average plus $(n + 1)d$.

sections.title: Exponents & roots
facts: $a^{-n} = \frac{1}{a^n}$ and $\left(\frac{p}{q}\right)^{-n} = \left(\frac{q}{p}\right)^{n}$: flipped, not negative.
$a^{\frac{m}{n}} = \left(\sqrt[n]{a}\right)^m$, so $27^{\frac{2}{3}} = 3^2 = 9$.
$\sqrt{a^2 b} = a\sqrt{b}$ and $\sqrt{a}\sqrt{b} = \sqrt{ab}$, but $\sqrt{a + b} \neq \sqrt{a} + \sqrt{b}$.
$2^{10} = 1024$. $2^n \cdot 5^n = 10^n$: use it to count digits.

sections.title: Clever arithmetic
facts: Near a round number: $99 \times 101 = 100^2 - 1$, and $n(n + 2) = (n + 1)^2 - 1$.
Take out common factors: $17 \times 23 + 17 \times 77 = 17 \times 100$, and $2^{20} + 2^{19} = 2^{19} \times 3$.
$(x - 1)(x + 1)(x^2 + 1)(x^4 + 1) = x^8 - 1$: multiply by $(x - 1)$ to start the chain.
